title: Arrays and index bounds
goal: Relate an index to the array length and check both bounds before reading an element.

prerequisites.text: Know how an || condition selects a branch and how return ends a function call.

terms.title: Array
terms.definition: A sequence of elements of one type. Its declaration gives the length explicitly or through a list of initial values.

terms.title: Index
terms.definition: The integer position of an element. The first element has index 0.

terms.title: Length
terms.definition: The number of elements. For an array of positive length n, the last valid index is n − 1.

sections.title: Position and value
paragraphs: A control panel has three zones numbered 0, 1 and 2. The levels array stores the setting for each zone in that order: 8, 4 and 9. A request for zone 2 selects the third position, which holds 9.
The list in braces supplies the initial values and fixes the length of levels. Dividing sizeof levels by sizeof levels[0] gives the element count while levels names the array itself.
Before evaluating levels[index], the program must establish that index is between 0 and length − 1. Check both bounds while index has the signed int type.
A boundary rejection is a control-flow check: `return` must happen before values[index] is read. A coincidental displayed value beyond the boundary cannot verify the program.

sections.title: Read a setting by zone number
paragraphs: The program calls show_level three times. Predict which calls reach the array read, then compare with the output below the listing.
steps: The call with 2 passes both checks. It reads levels[2] and prints 9.
The call with −1 fails the first check. The function prints invalid and returns.
The call with 3 fails the second check. The index equals the length, so the function returns before the array read.

sections.title: Why test the exact boundary?
paragraphs: If a test allows index <= length, supplying index equal to length exposes the error. Trace that condition on paper. Access outside the array has undefined behavior and can compile without a diagnostic.
The separate compiler example uses 1.5 in brackets. The compiler rejects that subscript because an index has integer type.

sections.title: Recalculate the boundary for a different panel
paragraphs: Imagine two zones with settings 6 and 10. Write down the valid indices. Choose tests for the last zone and the first position to its right, before evaluating any array access.

In the practice task the input numbers are already zero-based indices, so do not subtract one. Test index 3 separately: it denotes the fourth installation and must be accepted. Index 4 belongs to the rejection path even though it is only one higher.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Check the rules for subscripting and counting the elements of an array.

selfcheck.prompt: What does show_level(2) print for levels containing 8, 4 and 9?
What is the first index to the right of an array of length 4 that must give invalid?
feedback: Length 4 means indices 0, 1, 2 and 3 are valid.
Index 5 is invalid too. The first invalid index to the right is 4.

selfcheck.prompt: Which two checks guarantee safe access when length is 4? What happens for −1 and 4?
selfcheck.feedback: Reject index < 0 and index >= length. Input −1 triggers the first guard and input 4 triggers the second. In both cases the program returns before reading an element.

practice.title: Machine power by index
practice.task: Four machines have power ratings 12, 9, 15 and 4 at indices 0 through 3. Read a single integer index from the first line. Print the selected machine’s power on one line. Print invalid for a missing, malformed or out-of-range index. The supplied read_integer handles input, and any later lines are ignored. Fix the bounds check in main.
practice.hint: Find the last valid index for a four-element array. Compare it with the first index rejected by the condition.
criteria: Inputs -1 and 4 print invalid before any array access.
Missing or malformed input prints only invalid.

steps.action: Open Practice, leave 3 in the input box and select Run my code.
steps.why: Compare the starter’s output with the valid index range.
steps.expected: The starter prints invalid. The machine at index 3 should give 4.

steps.action: Fix the upper bound in main and run again with 3.
steps.why: Index 3 selects the last of four machines.

steps.action: Try -1, 4 and 0 in separate runs. Predict each result before running it.
steps.why: Check rejection on both sides and confirm that the first element still works.
steps.expected: The three outputs are invalid, invalid and 12.

exercises.title: Independent transfer
exercises.task: Save a local copy of your code in a text file. In the lesson editor, replace the power array with readings 20, 14, 6, 22 and 9. Find the last valid index and the first invalid one to its right. Restore your saved code after testing.
criteria: The length comes from the array, and 4 is the last valid index.
An input of 4 gives 9. An input of 5 gives invalid.

teaching.scene: A panel has three sectors with different levels. The operator enters a number and the program should show a level or report an invalid sector. Check both bounds before reading a cell.

predict.prompt: The levels are 8, 4 and 9, then the calls use 2, −1 and 3. Which call can read a cell, which are stopped, and which three lines appear?
predict.answer: Index 2 selects the third cell, holding 9. Both −1 and 3 are outside 0…2 and print invalid. The lines in order are 9, invalid, invalid.

apply.prompt: Another panel labels its four zones 5, 6, 2, and 8 with numbers 1 through 4, while the array still starts at index 0. What index does label 4 map to? How do you handle label 0 before reading an element?
apply.answer: First check that the label is between 1 and 4. A valid label of 4 maps to index 3 by subtracting 1, so the value is 8. Reject label 0 before calculating the index or reading an element.

practice.strategy: List the first and last valid indices and the nearest rejection at each end. Compare the starter condition with those four values before indexing the array.
practice.diagnosis: The starter gives invalid for index 3. For a four-value array, check whether the upper guard excludes the last valid position.

syntax.explanation: With positive length, valid indices run from 0 through length − 1. Checking both bounds before indexing keeps the operation within the array.
syntax.mistake: The condition `index > length` allows index equal to length. Trace it on paper and reject that index before reading.
